@emu.z88.card.rom.context: Cambridge Z88 card type: a ROM card. Shown in the Z88 slot strip under the emulator screen and in the Insert Card dialog's card-type list. Usually kept as is.

@emu.z88.card.ram.context: Cambridge Z88 card type: a RAM card. Shown in the Z88 slot strip under the emulator screen and, followed by its size (e.g. 'RAM 128K'), in the Insert Card dialog's card-type list. Usually kept as is.

@emu.z88.card.epromUv.context: Cambridge Z88 card type: a UV-erasable EPROM card. Shown in the Z88 slot strip and, followed by its size, in the Insert Card dialog's card-type list. Usually kept as is.

@emu.z88.card.intelFlash.context: Cambridge Z88 card type: an Intel flash memory card. Shown in the Z88 slot strip and, followed by its size, in the Insert Card dialog's card-type list. Only 'Flash' may need translating.

placeholders.chip: The chip's part number, e.g. '28F004S5' (never translated)

@emu.z88.card.amdFlash.context: Cambridge Z88 card type: an AMD flash memory card. Shown in the Z88 slot strip and, followed by its size, in the Insert Card dialog's card-type list. Only 'Flash' may need translating.

placeholders.chip: The chip's part number, e.g. '29F040B' (never translated)

emu.z88.slot.title: Slot {slot}:

@emu.z88.slot.title.context: Cambridge Z88 slot strip under the emulator screen: the label of a card slot, followed by the card's size (e.g. 'Slot 1: 128K').

@emu.z88.slot.ram.context: Cambridge Z88 slot strip: the internal RAM size of slot 0, e.g. '512K RAM'.

placeholders.size: The RAM size with its unit, e.g. '512K' (invariant)

@emu.z88.slot.empty.context: Cambridge Z88 slot strip: shown in place of the card size while a slot has no card.

@emu.z88.slot.romFile.context: Cambridge Z88 slot strip: the card type of a ROM card loaded from a file.

emu.media.dock.noBank: The file holds no DOCK bank

@emu.media.dock.noBank.context: Error shown when a Timex 2068 cartridge (.dck) file is inserted but contains no DOCK memory bank. Keep 'DOCK' (the Timex hardware name).

@emu.media.tape.errorTitle.context: Title of the message box shown when a tape file cannot be used.

emu.media.tape.notZx8081Program: {file} is not a ZX80/ZX81 program file

@emu.media.tape.notZx8081Program.context: Message box text: the chosen .p/.81/.o/.80 tape file is not a valid ZX80/ZX81 program.

emu.media.tape.ht1080z.highSpeed: {file} is a 1500-baud (Model III) tape; the HT-1080Z reads 500-baud tapes only.

@emu.media.tape.ht1080z.highSpeed.context: Message box text when a tape file cannot be put in the HT-1080Z's tape deck: the chosen .cas tape image was recorded at 1500 baud for the TRS-80 Model III, a speed the HT-1080Z's ROM cannot read. Keep "1500-baud", "500-baud" and "Model III".

emu.media.tape.ht1080z.noHeader: {file} has no 500-baud tape header, so it is not an HT-1080Z tape.

@emu.media.tape.ht1080z.noHeader.context: Message box text when a tape file cannot be put in the HT-1080Z's tape deck: the chosen .cas file does not contain the zero bytes and the sync byte that start every HT-1080Z / TRS-80 cassette recording.

emu.media.tape.ht1080z.cmdTruncated: {file} is cut short: a record runs past the end of the file.

@emu.media.tape.ht1080z.cmdTruncated.context: Message box text when a tape file cannot be put in the HT-1080Z's tape deck: the chosen .cmd machine-code file ends in the middle of one of its records.

emu.media.tape.ht1080z.cmdBadRecord: {file} contains a record type the HT-1080Z does not know.

@emu.media.tape.ht1080z.cmdBadRecord.context: Message box text when a tape file cannot be put in the HT-1080Z's tape deck: the chosen .cmd machine-code file contains a record of an unknown type.

emu.media.tape.ht1080z.cmdNoEntry: {file} has no start address, so the program cannot be started.

@emu.media.tape.ht1080z.cmdNoEntry.context: Message box text when a tape file cannot be put in the HT-1080Z's tape deck: the chosen .cmd machine-code file lacks the record that gives the address where the program starts.

@emu.media.tape.ht1080z.cmdNoCode.context: Message box text when a tape file cannot be put in the HT-1080Z's tape deck: the chosen .cmd machine-code file has no records with program bytes.

emu.media.tape.ht1080z.basNotTokenised: {file} is BASIC source text, not a tokenised HT-1080Z program. Only tokenised programs load from tape.

@emu.media.tape.ht1080z.basNotTokenised.context: Message box text when a tape file cannot be put in the HT-1080Z's tape deck: the chosen .bas file is not stored in the HT-1080Z's (TRS-80 Level II) tokenised BASIC format; it may be BASIC source text.

emu.media.tape.ht1080z.notTapeFile: {file} is not an HT-1080Z tape file (.cas, .cmd or .bas).

@emu.media.tape.ht1080z.notTapeFile.context: Message box text when a tape file cannot be put in the HT-1080Z's tape deck: the chosen file's extension is not one the HT-1080Z loads from tape. Keep the extensions as they are.

@emu.media.tape.errorMessage.context: Message box text: the tape file could not be read.

@emu.media.disk.ejectedMessage.context: Message box text confirming that a disk was ejected.

placeholders.drive: The drive letter, A or B (never translated)

@emu.media.disk.errorTitle.context: Title of the message box shown when a disk file cannot be used.

emu.debugRecording.discard.message: {action, select, stop {Stop discards what ran after the end of {recording}.} reset {Reset discards what ran after the end of {recording}.} other {Restart discards what ran after the end of {recording}.}}

@emu.debugRecording.discard.reset.context: Confirm button of the discard confirmation: resets the machine and discards the unsaved part of the recording.

@emu.debugRecording.discard.restart.context: Confirm button of the discard confirmation: restarts the machine and discards the unsaved part of the recording.

@emu.debugRecording.noKls.context: Error of opening a debug recording without its machine state section. Keep 'KLS' (a file section name).

@emu.debugRecording.opened.context: Emulator output line after a debug recording was opened; the program counter is appended in brackets.

emu.debugRecording.timelineNotStarted: The recording's timeline did not start

@emu.debugRecording.timelineNotStarted.context: Error of opening a debug recording: its reverse-debugging history could not be set up.

emu.debugRecording.overBudget: The recording is larger than the reverse-debugging memory budget: its oldest keyframes go as the machine runs on

@emu.debugRecording.overBudget.context: Warning after opening a debug recording bigger than the reverse-debugging memory budget.

emu.debugRecording.verifySkipped: -verify checks a recording opened at its present; it was opened in the past and not checked

@emu.debugRecording.verifySkipped.context: Warning of the open-recording command: its -verify option was ignored. Keep '-verify' (an option name).

emu.debugRecording.tape: The tape is the one in the recording ({file})

@emu.debugRecording.tape.context: Note after opening a debug recording: which tape the machine now has.

emu.debugRecording.disk: Disk {drive} is the one in the recording ({file}); it is detached from that file, so replaying never writes to it

@emu.debugRecording.disk.context: Note after opening a debug recording: the floppy disk comes from the recording.

placeholders.drive: The drive letter, A or B (never translated)

emu.debugRecording.sdCard.same: The SD card ({file}) is the one the recording was made with: running on past its end uses it

@emu.debugRecording.sdCard.same.context: Note after opening a ZX Spectrum Next debug recording made with the current SD card image.

placeholders.file: The SD card image's file name

emu.debugRecording.sdCard.other: Every SD card sector the recording read is in it, so it replays without the card; running on past its end uses the current card ({file}), which is not the recorded one ({recorded})

@emu.debugRecording.sdCard.other.context: Note after opening a ZX Spectrum Next debug recording made with another SD card image.

placeholders.file: The current SD card image's file name
placeholders.recorded: The recorded SD card image's file name

emu.debugRecording.sdCard.none: Every SD card sector the recording read is in it, so it replays without the card; running on past its end uses no card

@emu.debugRecording.sdCard.none.context: Note after opening a ZX Spectrum Next debug recording while no SD card image is set.

emu.debugRecording.sparse: The recording keeps only keyframes about a second apart: the first step back into a stretch replays longer

@emu.debugRecording.sparse.context: Note after opening a sparse debug recording (saved with -sparse).

emu.script.notCreated: Script {file} process has not been created.

@emu.script.notCreated.context: Script output (the script's output document): the emulator was asked to run a script the IDE has not registered.

@emu.script.started.context: Script output (the script's output document): the script began running in the emulator.

emu.script.completed: Script {file} with ID {id} completed in {ms, number} ms.

@emu.script.completed.context: Script output: the script finished normally.

emu.script.stopped: Script {file} with ID {id} stopped in {ms, number} ms.

@emu.script.stopped.context: Script output: the script was stopped by the user.

emu.script.failed: Script {file} with ID {id} failed in {ms, number} ms.

@emu.script.failed.context: Script output: the script ended with an error (the error follows on the next line).

@emu.script.unknownError.context: Script output: shown when a failed script's error has no text.

emu.script.notRunning: Script with ID {id} is not running.

@emu.script.notRunning.context: Script output: a stop was requested for a script that is not running.

@emu.script.stopping.context: Script output: the user asked to stop the script.

@panels.controls.registers.bitTooltip.context: Tooltip of one bit of an eight-bit flag strip in the register/state panels (e.g. the Z80 F register, a NextReg's flags): the bit number and what it means.

placeholders.description: What the bit means (may be empty)

@panels.controls.bankBrowser.filters.context: Accessible name (screen readers) of the filter buttons above a bank/block list in a file viewer (NEX, tape, snapshot, Z88).

panels.controls.bankBrowser.noMatch: {kind, select, block {No block matches this filter.} part {No part matches this filter.} other {No bank matches this filter.}}

@panels.controls.bankBrowser.noMatch.context: Empty state of a file viewer's bank/block list when the selected filter leaves nothing. Translate each branch; keep the select keywords (block, part, other) unchanged.

placeholders.kind: What the items are: block (tape blocks), part (program file parts), or bank (memory banks, the 'other' branch)

panels.controls.bankBrowser.listLabel: {kind, select, block {Block list} part {Part list} other {Bank list}}

@panels.controls.bankBrowser.listLabel.context: Accessible name (screen readers) of a file viewer's bank/block list. Translate each branch; keep the select keywords unchanged.

placeholders.kind: What the items are: block, part, or bank (the 'other' branch)

@panels.controls.bankBrowser.itemTitle.context: Title of the details pane of the selected bank/block in a file viewer, e.g. 'Bank $05'. Translate each branch; keep the select keywords unchanged.

placeholders.kind: What the items are: block, part, or bank (the 'other' branch)

@panels.controls.bankBrowser.detailsLabe.context: Accessible name (screen readers) of the details pane of the selected bank/block.

panels.controls.bankBrowser.rowHint: Double-click or Enter to pop out in {view}

@panels.controls.bankBrowser.rowHint.context: Tooltip of a row in a file viewer's bank/block list.

placeholders.view: The translated name of the view it opens in, e.g. 'Memory' or 'Disassembly'

panels.controls.bankBrowser.rowPopOut.ti: {kind, select, block {Pop out Block {number} ({view})} part {Pop out Part {number} ({view})} other {Pop out Bank {number} ({view})}}

@panels.controls.bankBrowser.rowPopOut.t.context: Tooltip of the pop-out icon on a row of a file viewer's bank/block list; it opens the item as its own document. Translate each branch; keep the select keywords unchanged.

placeholders.kind: What the items are: block, part, or bank (the 'other' branch)
placeholders.view: The translated name of the view it opens in

panels.controls.bankBrowser.rowPopOut.la: {kind, select, block {Pop out Block {number}} part {Pop out Part {number}} other {Pop out Bank {number}}}

@panels.controls.bankBrowser.rowPopOut.l.context: Accessible name (screen readers) of the pop-out icon on a row of a file viewer's bank/block list. Translate each branch; keep the select keywords unchanged.

placeholders.kind: What the items are: block, part, or bank (the 'other' branch)

panels.controls.bankBrowser.openAsDocume: {kind, select, block {Open this block as its own document} part {Open this part as its own document} other {Open this bank as its own document}}

@panels.controls.bankBrowser.openAsDocum.context: Tooltip of the 'Pop out' button in the details pane of a file viewer's selected bank/block. Translate each branch; keep the select keywords unchanged.

placeholders.kind: What the items are: block, part, or bank (the 'other' branch)

@panels.controls.bankBrowser.popOut.context: Text of the button in the details pane that opens the selected bank/block as its own document; the view's name follows it after a dot.

@panels.controls.bankBrowser.popOutIn.context: Accessible name (screen readers) of the 'Pop out' button in the details pane of a file viewer.

placeholders.view: The translated name of the view it opens in, e.g. 'Memory'

@panels.controls.bankBrowser.menuPopOutI.context: Context-menu item of a bank/block in a file viewer (title case, like other menu items): opens it as its own document in that view.

placeholders.view: The translated name of the view it opens in, e.g. 'Memory'

@panels.controls.bankBrowser.popOutOther.context: Tooltip and accessible name of the arrow button beside 'Pop out' that opens a menu of the other views.

@panels.controls.bankBrowser.lastUsed.context: Grey note at the right of the menu item for the view a bank/block was last popped out in.

panels.controls.nextPalette.label: Next palette

@panels.controls.nextPalette.label.context: Accessible name (screen readers) of the ZX Spectrum Next palette grid (256 colour swatches) in the palette panels and editors.

@panels.controls.nextPalette.tooltip.context: Tooltip of a swatch in the ZX Spectrum Next palette grid: the palette index and its red/green/blue components. R, G and B may be replaced by your language's usual abbreviations.

placeholders.index: The palette index in hex, e.g. '$1F'

@panels.controls.nextPalette.tooltipWith.context: Tooltip of a swatch in the ZX Spectrum Next palette grid that has special roles, listed in brackets.

placeholders.index: The palette index in hex, e.g. '$1F'
placeholders.flags: The roles, e.g. 'priority, transparency' (translated, joined by the separator message)

@panels.controls.nextPalette.flag.priori.context: Role of a ZX Spectrum Next palette entry, listed in its tooltip: the Layer 2 priority bit is set (the colour is drawn above the other layers). Lower case, as it appears inside brackets.

@panels.controls.nextPalette.flag.transp.context: Role of a ZX Spectrum Next palette entry, listed in its tooltip: this index is the transparent colour. Lower case, as it appears inside brackets.

@panels.controls.nextPalette.flagSeparat.context: Separator between the roles listed in a palette swatch's tooltip (e.g. 'priority, transparency'). Keep the trailing space if your language uses one.

@panels.controls.spriteSheet.bytesMark.context: Accessible name (screen readers) of the mark on a sprite pattern that the user marked as data bytes, not a picture (NEX viewer and sprite inspector).

@panels.controls.spriteSheet.mixedFormat.context: Accessible name of the warning mark on a sprite pattern whose data is used as both 8-bit and 4-bit patterns.

@panels.controls.spriteSheet.uploadCurso.context: Accessible name of the mark on the sprite pattern the next pattern upload (port $5B) writes into.

@panels.controls.spriteSheet.selectedSpr.context: Accessible name of the mark on the pattern the selected sprite shows.

@panels.controls.spriteSheet.zoom.context: Accessible name of the group of zoom buttons (1×-4×) above a sprite pattern sheet.

@panels.controls.dropdown.placeholder.context: Placeholder of a drop-down list while nothing is chosen (used when the caller sets no placeholder of its own).

emu.ht1080z.code.empty: The build has no code to put into the HT-1080Z.

@emu.ht1080z.code.empty.context: Error when building code for the HT-1080Z (a Hungarian school computer) produced no bytes.

emu.ht1080z.code.rom: Code at {address} is in the HT-1080Z's ROM or keyboard area (below $3C00) and cannot be loaded. Put it in RAM; $7000 is a good place.

@emu.ht1080z.code.rom.context: Error: assembled code lies where the HT-1080Z has ROM or its keyboard, so it cannot be written. $3C00 and $7000 are addresses: keep them.

emu.ht1080z.code.beyondRam: Code at {address} is beyond the RAM of this {ramKb}K HT-1080Z. Keep it below $8000, or choose a 48K model.

@emu.ht1080z.code.beyondRam.context: Error: assembled code is above the end of the running HT-1080Z's memory.

placeholders.ramKb: The machine's memory in kilobytes: 16 or 48

emu.ht1080z.code.tooLow: Code at {address} leaves BASIC less than 1K of memory. Put it at {lowest} or above; $7000 is a good place.

@emu.ht1080z.code.tooLow.context: Error: assembled code starts so low in the HT-1080Z's memory that BASIC would have no room left.

emu.media.microdrive.title: Microdrive {drive}

@emu.media.microdrive.title.context: ZX Spectrum media strip under the emulator screen: the name of a Microdrive card (the ZX Interface 1's tape-cartridge drives), shown as the tooltip and accessible name of its icon.

@emu.media.microdrive.empty.context: ZX Spectrum media strip: shown in place of the file name while a Microdrive is empty.

@emu.media.microdrive.running.context: ZX Spectrum media strip: tooltip of a Microdrive card's icon while the emulated machine has the drive's motor running.
